BiblicalUsage: Chadah means to rejoice, to be glad. Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness the LORD had done to Israel, the king is made exceeding glad with God's countenance, and Job turns the word dark — wishing the night of his birth had never been glad, never been counted among the days of the year.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe gladness is the natural sound of a heart that has seen God's goodness, and Job's wish shows what sorrow does to it. Joy is the first thing grief tries to take, and the last thing God restores.
